The '''2026 Worthing Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026, alongside the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day, to elect 14 of 29 members of [[Worthing Borough Council]] in [[West Sussex]], [[England]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=mhclgpress |date=2026-02-16 |title=Update on May 2026 local authority elections – MHCLG in the Media |url=https://mhclgmedia.blog.gov.uk/2026/02/16/update-on-may-2026-local-authority-elections/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=mhclgmedia.blog.gov.uk |language=en}}</ref>

==Summary==

===Background===
In [[2024 Worthing Borough Council election|2024]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] won majority control of the council.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Worthing result - Local Elections 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000229 |access-date=2026-02-17 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> In January 2026, the council asked for the election to be postponed pending local government reorganisation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-06 |title=Councillors demand urgent meeting over risk to 2026 local elections |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/25738941.worthing-councillors-call-urgent-talks-2026-elections/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=The Argus |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-09 |title=Will Sussex get to vote in 2026 or will elections be called off? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cn567we03v1o |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> However it was rescheduled on 16 February 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-16 |title=Elections back on across Sussex after government U-turn |url=https://www.brightonandhovenews.org/2026/02/16/elections-back-on-across-sussex-after-government-u-turn/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=Brighton and Hove News |language=en-US}}</ref>

Changes 2024–2026:
*May 2024: Margaret Howard (Labour), Hilary Schan (Labour), and Carl Walker (Labour) leave party to sit as independents<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicholson |first1=Savannah |title=Councillors break with Labour to become independents |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/24309400.worthing-councillors-leave-labour-become-independents/ |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=The Argus |date=10 May 2024 |language=en}}</ref>
*July 2024: [[Beccy Cooper]] (Labour) resigns – by-election held September 2024<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boothroyd |first1=David |title=Three Rivers Lib Dems are two down |url=https://www.localcouncils.co.uk/2024/07/three-rivers-lib-dems-are-two-down/ |website=LocalCouncils.co.uk |access-date=5 May 2026}}</ref>
*August 2024: Richard Mulholland (Labour) resigns – by-election held October 2024<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hunt |first1=Lucy |title=Second council by-election due as councillor resigns |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/24539192.second-worthing-by-election-due-heene-councillor-resigns/ |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=The Argus |date=25 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref>
*September 2024: Thomas Taylor (Conservative) gains by-election from Labour<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Marine Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/5426/#2024-09-19 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=5 May 2026}}</ref>
*October 2024: Luke Houghton (Conservative) gains by-election from Labour<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Heene Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/5425/#2024-10-10 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=5 May 2026}}</ref>
*May 2025: Luke Houghton (Conservative) joins Reform<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hunt |first1=Lucy |title=Tory councillor defects to Reform in shock move dubbed 'breach of trust' by leader |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/25192618.worthing-conservative-councillor-defects-reform-uk/ |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=The Argus |date=27 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
*November 2025: Charles James (Conservative) joins Reform<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicholson |first1=Savannah |title=Councillor defects to Reform UK |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/25636628.worthing-councillor-charles-james-defects-reform-uk/ |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=The Argus |date=20 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
